title: Processing of identified registration data
description: Authentication service processes identified data including name, email address, and government ID provided during parent registration.

title: Collection of sensitive government ID
description: Highly sensitive government ID data type is collected and processed for registration, exceeding minimal functional needs for authentication.

title: Excessive volume of personal data in registration
description: Multiple personal data items (email, password, name, govt ID, six-digit code) are processed beyond basic authentication requirements.

title: Violation of data minimization in registration flow
description: More personal data including sensitive govt ID is collected than strictly necessary for parent registration and authentication.

title: Attributable registration data evidence
description: The act of submitting identifiable registration data creates attributable evidence that the parent user cannot later deny.

title: Linking parent accounts via unique identifiers
description: The Authentication Service shares parent account data containing unique identifiers (e.g. username, email or internal ID) which enables linking of this data to the individual.
assumptions: Parent account data includes at least one unique identifier as is standard for authentication storage.

title: Linking via stored unique identifiers in users collection
description: MongoDB users collection receives and stores parent account records using unique identifiers, allowing future linking of activities or data to specific parents.
assumptions: Standard account storage uses unique keys or indexed identifiers.

title: Sending identified parent account data
description: Authentication Service processes and transmits identified personal data (parent accounts) to be stored.

title: Storing identified information in users collection
description: The MongoDB datastore receives and persists identified parent account data.

title: Account data record attributable to parent
description: The data flow carries account data that creates an attributable record preventing the parent from denying the account creation or associated claims.

title: Retention of parent account data
description: Personal parent account data is stored in the MongoDB collection, potentially retained longer than strictly necessary without specified deletion policies.
assumptions: No retention period mentioned in flow.
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not specify retention details so this is inferred from typical storage behavior.

title: Unawareness of parent account storage
description: Parents may be unaware that their account data is being stored by the Authentication Service in the users collection.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation for parent accounts
description: Storing parent account data without clear time limits may violate storage limitation principles under regulations like GDPR.
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual retention policy not provided in flow description.

title: Identifier in JWT
description: The JWT in the flow contains a unique subject identifier linking the token to a specific user identity.

title: Signed data evidence
description: JWT is cryptographically signed by the Authentication Service, creating attributable evidence of the authentication event and claims that cannot be repudiated.

title: Disclosure of user data
description: User data is disclosed by the Authentication Service along with the JWT, which may include sensitive or unnecessary personal details for the parent recipient.

title: Unique identifier linking
description: JWT contains unique identifiers that can link the data flow to a specific parent user across sessions or contexts.

title: Child shares identified parent credentials
description: The child user (EE2) shares parent email and password for login, which is identified information being transmitted from the source.

title: Transmission of highly sensitive password data
description: The data flow carries parent password, a highly sensitive data type that requires strict protection during transit for child login authentication.

title: Child unawareness of parental data processing
description: The child user may be unaware that their login action involves processing and potential storage of parent's personal data (email/password) by the authentication service.

title: Potential invalid consent for child login
description: Authentication service processes child login using parent credentials, risking invalid or unverifiable consent under child data protection rules like GDPR/COPPA.

title: JWT contains unique child identifier
description: The JWT token includes a unique reference (e.g. subject claim or user ID) to the child data subject, making the transmitted data identifiable.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child profile data
description: Authentication service shares child profiles which constitute highly sensitive personal data of minors, beyond basic authentication needs.

title: Potential unlawful processing of child data
description: Sending child profiles and JWTs with userType child may involve processing children's personal data without ensuring valid consent or appropriate lawful basis specific to minors.
uncertainty_note: Child-specific regulations (e.g. GDPR Art. 8, COPPA) require heightened scrutiny; exact consent mechanism not specified in flow.

title: Sharing of identified child data
description: Parent user shares child's name, DOB, gender and government ID to create profile, directly providing identified personal data.

title: Processing of identified child data
description: Child Profile Management process receives and handles identified data including government ID for child profile creation.

title: Linking via government ID
description: Government ID serves as unique identifier allowing linking of the child's profile data to the individual.

title: Sensitive data type collection for child profile
description: Government ID is a highly sensitive data type collected for child profile creation, which may exceed strict functional necessity or increase risk.
uncertainty_note: Whether govt ID is strictly required depends on system context not fully specified in flow.

title: Child data subject unawareness
description: Child (data subject) is likely unaware of the collection and processing of their personal data (name, DOB, gender, govt ID) by the profile management system, as interaction is via parent.

title: Invalid or inadequate consent for child data
description: Processing of child's government ID and other personal data may lack valid consent mechanisms or proper verification of parental authority under regulations like GDPR.
uncertainty_note: Specific consent flows not described in this data flow.

title: Storage of identified child profile data
description: The MongoDB datastore receives and stores identified personal data about children as part of the store/update child profile flow.

title: Sensitive child data types stored
description: Child profile data includes highly sensitive personal information (minors) that is stored in the collection, with potential for sensitivity beyond minimal functional needs if profiles are detailed.
uncertainty_note: Child data is inherently sensitive per regulations; granularity not specified in flow.

title: Potential violation of storage limitation for child profiles
description: Child profiles stored without specified retention limits may violate storage limitation principles, especially for minor data subjects.
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not specify retention policies.

title: Lack of rectification control in profile updates
description: The process updating child profiles may not provide data subjects (or guardians) sufficient control for rectification or erasure of profile data.

title: Child data subject unawareness of processing
description: The child user sharing video search, requests, likes and comments may not understand or be aware of the collection, processing and storage of their personal interaction data by the service.

title: Invalid consent for child personal data

title: Profiling child through interaction data
description: The service can analyze patterns in the child's video searches, likes and comments to profile the individual and link future data or actions to them.

title: Identified information in video metadata
description: The metadata of video files or communication involves identified information when stored in the MongoDB videos collection.

title: Data propagation to datastore
description: Video metadata and files are propagated to the datastore which may not be strictly needed beyond storage.
uncertainty_note: No explicit evidence of unnecessary propagation in the flow description.

title: Violation of storage limitation
description: Personal video data may be stored longer than functionally needed in the MongoDB collection.
uncertainty_note: Flow description provides no details on retention policies.

title: Profiling via watch and search history storage
description: Storing child search and watch history in the childprofiles collection enables detailed profiling of individual children's viewing patterns and preferences, linking actions to specific profiles over time.

title: Identifier-linked child history
description: The childprofiles datastore receives and stores search/watch history tied to unique child identifiers or profile references, making the data identifiable.

title: Sensitive child behavioral data collection
description: Watch and search history of children represents highly sensitive personal data (behavioral profiling of minors) that is being stored without clear indication of strict functional necessity in the given flow.

title: Child data consent and lawfulness issues
description: Storing children's search and watch history in persistent profiles raises risks of invalid or insufficient consent under GDPR for processing children's personal data.

title: Unawareness of child data storage
description: The Child Profile Management process shares search/watch history for storage, but data subjects (children or guardians) may be unaware of the extent of collection and long-term profiling implications.

title: Video encoding includes metadata
description: The video file encoding or format may include additional personal data (e.g. metadata, timestamps, device info) not strictly needed for approval/rejection functionality.
assumptions: Video files typically carry metadata unless explicitly stripped.
uncertainty_note: Flow description does not specify if metadata is present or stripped before upload.

title: Parent user unaware of downstream processing
description: The parent user uploading the video may be unaware of how the Video Management Service will process, store, or use the video for approval/rejection decisions.

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: If the full video is retained or analyzed beyond what is minimally required for the approval/rejection decision, this could violate minimization principles.
uncertainty_note: Insufficient details on retention or analysis practices in the flow description.

title: Sensitive child data type shared
description: MongoDB childprofiles shares highly sensitive child browsing data to the AI engine beyond minimal needs.

title: Invalid consent for AI processing of child data
description: Planned flow of child browsing data to AI engine risks lacking valid parental consent under GDPR.

title: Data subjects unaware of flow to AI

title: Browsing data shared with predetermined advertisers

title: Profiling individuals via received browsing data
description: Third-party advertisers can analyze browsing data to profile individuals and link activities to specific users.

title: Quasi-identifiers enabling identification by advertisers
description: Browsing data received by advertisers may include quasi-identifiers allowing re-identification of data subjects.

title: Data subjects unaware of browsing data sharing
description: Users whose browsing data is processed by the AI engine are likely unaware of its planned disclosure to advertisers.

title: Potential invalid consent for data sharing to advertisers

title: Storage of identified government ID data
description: The destination file system stores government ID images which constitute identified personal data including photos, names, numbers and other direct identifiers.

title: Storage of highly sensitive data type
description: Government ID images represent a highly sensitive data type (official identity documents) being persisted in the backend/uploads/ datastore, with elevated disclosure risks.

title: Processing of special-category personal data
description: Storing government-issued ID images likely involves special category data (e.g. biometric elements or official documents) without evident additional safeguards or lawful basis considerations.

title: JWT contains unique user identifier
description: The Authentication Service includes a unique subject identifier (e.g. 'sub' claim) in the JWT that is then stored, allowing identification of the data subject.

title: Broad accessibility of stored JWT
description: Storing the JWT in browser localStorage makes the personal data (claims) accessible to any JavaScript running on the page or potentially browser extensions, exposing it more broadly than necessary.

title: Signed JWT prevents deniability
description: The signed JWT stored in localStorage serves as attributable evidence of user actions or identity claims that the data subject cannot easily repudiate.

title: Unique identifier enables linking
description: The JWT in transit and storage carries a unique identifier that can link authentication events and user data across sessions or contexts.

title: Disclosure of sensitive child history data
description: Child history retrieved and sent to parent may include highly sensitive personal data types about a minor beyond what is strictly necessary for review.

title: Child data subject unawareness

title: Unlawful processing of child personal data
